**CH-28.** The step-2 mass audit is run on every batch. If the total recorded output mass exceeds the total recorded input mass, then the audit has failed and conservation of mass has been violated somewhere in the record. For batch PR-14-03 the recorded input mass was 46.60 g (25.00 g salicylic acid plus 21.60 g acetic anhydride) and the recorded output masses total 45.02 g (26.85 g isolated product plus 18.17 g recovered filtrate solids), so the outputs do not exceed the inputs and no conservation violation is indicated; the 1.58 g difference, 3.4 per cent of the charge, sits within the 5 per cent handling-loss allowance.
====
**CH-28.** The step-2 mass audit is run on every batch. All output streams — including the liquid by‑product — must be recorded and summed. If the total recorded output mass exceeds the total recorded input mass, conservation of mass has been violated and the audit fails. If the total recorded output mass is less than the total recorded input mass, the absolute shortfall must not exceed the 5 per cent handling‑loss allowance; otherwise the audit fails due to unaccounted loss. For batch PR-14-03 the recorded input mass was 46.60 g (25.00 g salicylic acid plus 21.60 g acetic anhydride) and the recorded output masses total 45.02 g (26.85 g isolated product plus 18.17 g recovered filtrate solids). The outputs do not exceed the inputs, and the 1.58 g shortfall (3.4 per cent of the charge) sits within the 5 per cent handling‑loss allowance; however, the liquid by‑product mass was not independently recorded, so the audit cannot exclude the possibility that an unrecorded liquid stream contributes to the apparent 3.4 per cent shortfall. The audit therefore passes conditionally, pending explicit inclusion of the liquid output mass in the output records.
